title: Derived pushforward and pullback of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes, with the functors $f_*=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ
\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)$ and $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ
\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ on module objects
([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]). The derived pushforward and pullback are
the *total derived functors of these composites* ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]):

$$
Rf_*:=R\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\bigr)
\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}),
$$

computed on K-injective resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, with bounded below version
$R^+f_*\colon D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$, and

$$
Lf^*:=L\bigl(\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\bigr)
\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}),
$$

computed on K-flat resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$: for a K-flat resolution
$P\to M$ one has $Lf^*M\cong\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}P$. They are the general
derived functors applied to the underived functors, not separate constructions; in
particular they are not built from the derived functors of abelian sheaves. The
adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ derives to an adjunction

$$
Lf^*\dashv Rf_* .
$$

The composite is derived, rather than the factors, because the derived adjunction is
then obtained directly from $f^*\dashv f_*$ (a composite of derived functors would
require composing two derived adjunctions through an intermediate category), and
because the universal property of derived functors then applies to the functor one
cares about. The factorizations of $Rf_*$ and $Lf^*$ through the factors are kept as
theorems, proved below.

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, work on the small skeleton of $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and put $\mathcal C_T=\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the constant ring sheaf $\mathbf Z$: a sheaf of abelian groups has a unique compatible $\mathbf Z$-action, given by repeated addition, and every additive map preserves it. Thus $\mathcal C_T$ is Grothendieck abelian. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] it has the closed symmetric sheafified tensor product, with tensoring on either side preserving colimits. In particular tensoring preserves zero objects and finite biproducts and is additive: the sum of maps is the composite of their biproduct with diagonal and codiagonal.

Let $\mathbf Z_U$ be the sheafified free abelian presheaf on an object $U$ of this site. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat] with $P=\mathbf Z$, tensoring with $\mathbf Z_U$ preserves finite limits, since tensoring with $\mathbf Z$ is the identity. It preserves cokernels by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], hence is exact; symmetry gives the other tensor functor. Set $P_T(M)=\bigoplus_{(U,s),\ s\in M(U)}\mathbf Z_U$. A morphism $h:M\to N$ maps the summand $(U,s)$ identically to $(U,h_U(s))$, which defines a functor. On the summand $(U,s)$, define evaluation before sheafification by sending the generator indexed by $\varphi:V\to U$ to $M(\varphi)(s)\in M(V)$. For $\psi:V'\to V$, the equality $M(\varphi\psi)(s)=M(\psi)(M(\varphi)(s))$ proves compatibility with restrictions, so the map extends uniquely to the sheafification and then to the coproduct. The equality $h_V(M(\varphi)(s))=N(\varphi)(h_U(s))$ proves naturality in $M$. Evaluation $P_T(M)\to M$ is surjective on sections: $s\in M(U)$ is the image of the identity generator in the summand $(U,s)$. It is therefore an epimorphism, since two maps out of $M$ agreeing after evaluation agree on every section. Each $P_T(M)$ is flat: tensor distributes over its coproduct by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and direct sums of exact sequences are exact, being filtered colimits of their finite subsums; the filtered-colimit exactness is in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Thus $P_T$ with evaluation supplies functorial flat resolutions in $\mathcal C_T$.

source.place: Part 4: the functorial epimorphism from the sum of free abelian sheaves

proof.text: The coefficient $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] defines $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ as its module-object category in $\mathcal C_T$. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor], and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] to obtain its closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian structure. All their ambient hypotheses hold by step 1, including coequalizers and preservation of colimits by tensor. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] using step 2 to obtain functorial flat resolutions. Closedness and symmetry make both relative tensor functors left adjoints, so they preserve colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. In particular they preserve finite biproducts and are additive by the diagonal-codiagonal formula from step 1. The Grothendieck property supplies countable coproducts and exact filtered colimits; $(\mathbf Z,\leq)$ is filtered since any two integers have a common upper bound. Consequently its colimits are exact and preserved by tensor, which verifies every structural hypothesis of the left-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

source.place: Parts 3 and 4: module structures and the hypotheses for K-flat resolutions

proof.text: The pushforward clause of the current [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identifies the functor in the item with the functor of [def-sfb-module-lower-star]: it is the full composite $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f_*^{\Ab})$ and is additive. By step 3 its source is Grothendieck abelian, so [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] gives K-injective resolutions and the total right derived functor $Rf_*$. For a K-injective resolution $M\to I$, it is computed by $f_*I$. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] the source also has enough injectives; applying [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] gives $R^+f_*:D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$, computed on bounded below complexes of injectives. The compatibility isomorphism of [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility], applied to this additive $f_*$ with the enough-injectives and K-injective-resolution hypotheses just checked, identifies this functor after inclusion with the restriction of $Rf_*$ to $D^+$.

source.place: Proof paragraph: existence and resolution computation of R(f_*) and R^+(f_*)

proof.text: The current definition [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identifies the pullback as the full composite $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ and records its tensor formula; [def-sfb-module-upper-star] gives the same formula and additivity in detail. By [lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso] it sends quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms. With step 3, the left-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] therefore constructs $Lf^*$ on the unbounded derived categories, computed on K-flat resolutions. For $P\to M$ such a resolution, $Lf^*M$ is represented by $f^*P$. Applying the explicit formula in [def-sfb-module-upper-star] in every degree, including the differentials, identifies this representative with $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}P$.

source.place: Proof paragraph: existence of L(f^*) and the displayed K-flat computation

proof.text: The adjunction clause of the current [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] states $f^*\dashv f_*$ for exactly the full composites in steps 4 and 5, using that $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$. Apply the derived-adjunction clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] with $\mathcal C=\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$, $\mathcal D=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, left functor $f^*$ and right functor $f_*$. Step 3 supplies the left source's monoidal and flat-resolution hypotheses and the right source's K-injective resolutions; steps 4 and 5 give additivity of both functors and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes by $f^*$. This yields $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ for the functors already constructed, exactly the adjunction specified in [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. The coefficient maps in this application have their abelian-sheaf meaning: $\alpha_f:f^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ and $\eta_f:\Lambda_Y\to f_*^{\Ab}\Lambda_X$. Extension along $\alpha_f$ remains part of $f^*$, without choosing an inverse. All total derived constructions therefore apply to the module composites themselves, as asserted; no factorization through derived abelian-sheaf functors is used.
